title: Spine Event Envelope
description: The fleet's published language: the envelope every event wears. Senders mint `id`; the Spine assigns `seq` and `acceptedAt` on append (they are absent at submission, present in the log). See contracts/README.md for the versioning policy.

id.description: Sender-minted GUID. Idempotency key: the Spine elides a retried duplicate.

tableId.description: Which table's log. Pre-Spine, the table name IS the id (unique among active tables) — no format constraint. Once the Spine mints a GUID at table creation, this field becomes that GUID and the name reverts to a lookup alias in the table.created payload.

seq.description: Spine-assigned on append: authoritative order within the log. Senders must not set this.

name.description: The event's kind, namespaced (e.g. card.played). Determines which payload schema applies.

acceptedAt.description: Spine-assigned on append: the Spine's clock, when the log accepted it. Senders must not set this.

occurredAt.description: Optional. The initiator app's clock, when physics preceded ingestion.

initiator.description: Who made this happen: a seated player, a named spectator, later the interpreter.

seatId.description: Present when a seated player made this happen. Absent for a named spectator or other non-seated initiator.

playerName.description: Display only. Not unique, not an identity.

occurredIn.description: Which application recorded/sent it. `interpreter` joins this enum later.

origin.description: One level more specific than `occurredIn`: which mechanism, within that app, minted this event (e.g. `shuffler.playCardSubmit`, `spine.seatTaken`, `tabletop.cardShapeHook`). An open, dot-namespaced string like `name` — not a closed enum, so a new call site anywhere in the fleet never needs a schema change first. Unlike `name` (fully lowercase), segments after the first app name may be camelCase, since a mechanism name (`tableLookupMiss`, `playCardSubmit`) reads naturally that way. Hard-coded literal, one per mint site.

significance.description: What kind of fact this event states, independent of which app or mechanism produced it. `physical` — a card moved, hand sorting, a note/annotation on the table; raw motion/arrangement, meaning-free. `domain` — a real game-related fact (a card is drawn, played, or moved to a zone). `administrative` — table/seat bookkeeping (table.created, seat.taken, seat.joined), not gameplay itself.

traceparent.description: W3C trace context for this event, carried on the envelope itself rather than only a transport header — the outbound SSE stream has no header to ride, and a future batched `sendEvent` would otherwise lose per-event trace context. Optional: tracing is best-effort and must never be the reason an event is rejected. Observability only — traces expire (~60d); durable causality between events uses `id` references, never trace ids. The Spine's persisted log does not keep this field; it's attached fresh whenever an event is broadcast live.

schemaVersion.description: Integer version of this `name`'s payload schema.

payload.description: The kind-specific body, validated against payloads/<name>.v<schemaVersion>.json.
